28:37 photographs showed exactly what they’d seen that  day. They said they’d originally hesitated to make

28:42 the images public because they feared the object  might’ve been part of a secret military project.

28:47 And there was another image  that would become legendary.

28:51 11. One of the FBI documents dated June 8th,

28:54 1967, shows us that a man named Paul Peyerl  provided the agency information that possibly

29:00 proved the Nazis had built a UFO. Peyerl claimed  he saw it hover above the Black Forest in 1944.

29:07 The now declassified document states: “During this period, he observed the

29:11 aircraft described above. It was disc-shaped…  remotely controlled, and equipped with several

29:16 jet engines on the outer part of the structure.” The machine had an outer section that spun

29:21 around a central dome, while the  rest of it remained stationary.

29:24 It’s interesting that the UFOs people often  see looked exactly like the ones in sci-fi

29:29 movies. But Peyerl took a picture.  All that remains of it is a Xerox

29:33 copy of this negative, so it’s not very clear. The hardest events to explain are those in which

29:39 several people saw the same thing. 10.

29:42 On February 10th, 1951, just before 1 a.m., a  U.S. Navy Douglas R5D transport plane carrying

29:50 31 people crossed the skies above Keflavík  when the crew spotted something impossible.

29:55 Roughly 1,500 feet (457 meters) above the  ocean, a strange glowing object appeared

30:00 beneath them. It was silent, bright, and  moving in ways they couldn’t explain.

30:04 Everyone onboard reportedly saw it. A disc-shaped object with an orange-red glow

30:09 around its perimeter. As the object drew closer,  the pilots said their instruments began to fail.

30:15 The heading indicator malfunctioned, along with  the magnetic compass and two direction finders.

30:20 Then, as the aircraft moved away from the object,  the instruments suddenly returned to normal.

30:25 The incident remained classified for years, but  surviving documents suggest Navy intelligence

30:30 took the encounter seriously. Roughly 9 months  later, investigators reportedly visited the pilot

30:35 and showed him what amounted to a police lineup  of UFO photographs, asking whether any matched

30:41 what he’d seen that night over the Atlantic. This wasn’t some publicity-seeker or eccentric

30:46 chasing fame. He was a trusted military pilot  whose account was treated as credible by the

30:51 people investigating it. Just like this next man.

30:54 9. Again in 1951,

30:57 L. Gordon Cooper was flying his F-86 Thunderjet  in Germany when he saw a group of objects moving

31:03 in ways not possible with human engineering. He would later work for NASA in Project Mercury,

31:08 the US’s first space program. He  was smart and trustworthy. So when

31:13 he told his superiors he’d seen a metallic  silver saucer in the sky, people listened.

31:17 After retiring from NASA with the rank of  colonel and 222 hours in space under his belt,

31:23 he wrote a book claiming the government was  actively suppressing information about UFOS.

31:28 He detailed a separate incident in 1957 where his  crew had captured footage of a landed saucer at

31:34 a California Air Force base. When he handed  the film over to Washington, everything went

31:38 quiet. He was locked out of his own story. Until his dying breath, he was certain the

31:44 government was involved in a UFO cover-up. Some stories were just too crazy to rationally

31:49 explain. 8.

31:51 Over the years, there have been claims that  the CIA used UFOs as a form of misdirection.

31:56 There may be some truth to that idea, but the  declassified documents show us a more complicated

32:01 picture. Some people within the CIA were, on  paper, deeply concerned about what it saw as

32:06 the public’s growing gullibility and how hostile  powers might exploit it. Some files even discussed

32:12 the danger of Soviet-engineered mass hysteria  or psychological warfare built around UFO panic.

32:18 One document stated the agency needed to “reduce  the current gullibility of the public and

32:23 consequently their susceptibility to propaganda.” That concern helped lead to the creation of the

32:28 Robertson Panel in 1953,backed by the CIA and  chaired by Howard P. Robertson, one of the most

32:34 respected physicists in the world. Its mission  was straightforward: investigate the flying saucer

32:39 phenomenon and debunk it once and for all. And when the panel finally got to work,

32:44 this is what happened. 7.

32:46 The same year the panel was convened, a major  stationed at George Air Force Base in California

32:51 reported seeing 5 enormous disc-shaped  objects flying in formation above the base.

32:57 And he was far from the only witness. Over the next 12 weeks, 9 more

33:00 sightings of similar objects were  reported at the same installation.

33:04 Then, on the very same day the major witnessed  the discs, military personnel at Davis-Monthan

33:10 Air Force Base in Arizona reported something  equally weird. 12 unidentified objects flying in

33:16 formation at estimated speeds of between 1,500  and 2,000 miles per hour (2,414 - 3,218 kph).

33:21 It was the kind of performance that was beyond  anything publicly known to exist in the 1950s.

33:27 The legendary Lockheed SR-71  Blackbird wouldn’t emerge from

33:31 the secret world of Area 51 until the mid-1960s. And these super-fast vehicle sightings weren’t

33:37 only confined to the US. 6.

33:39 In September 1953, NATO warships participating  in Operation Mainbrace were crossing the North

33:44 Atlantic. During the mission, a Danish  naval commander and his crew reported

33:49 a glowing triangular object tearing across the  sky at roughly 900 miles per hour (1,448 kph).

33:54 It was also glowing with an eerie blue light. Over the following weeks, more sightings

33:59 emerged from personnel involved in the  exercise. None of them were explained.

34:03 Then right after came an incident in Yorkshire,  northern England. RAF personnel reported that

34:08 an unidentified object appeared to shadow one of  their Meteor jet fighters in flight. One airman

34:14 later described the object as a silver disc. “It stopped its descent and hung in the air,

34:19 rotating as if on its own axis,” he said. “Then it  accelerated at an incredible speed to the West.”

34:25 But what happened when investigators believed  they’d found not just a sighting, but actual

34:30 physical evidence? 5.

34:32 Arthur Stansel, a technician connected to the  Nevada Test Site, would later become part of

34:37 UFO legend. In a sworn statement, he claimed  that on May 21st 1953, he’d helped recover part

34:43 of a crashed UFO near Kingman, Arizona. According to his account, the object was

34:49 “constructed of an unfamiliar metal which  resembled brushed aluminum.” He said he and

34:54 several other men dug it out of the sand where  it had partially embedded itself after impact.

34:58 The craft, he claimed, was oval-shaped, roughly 30  feet (9 meters) in diameter, with two swivel seats

35:04 and a cabin filled with strange instruments. He later described it as something so many

35:08 people had seen all over the world – “a  teardrop-shaped cigar... a streamlined cigar.”

35:14 Then came the detail that would one day  make Americans feel like they weren’t alone.

35:18 “A tent pitched near the object sheltered the  dead remains of the only occupant,” he stated.

35:24 Occupant, as in… alien. So what exactly had Stansel claimed to have seen?

35:29 In his own words, the being was  “about 4 feet (1.21 meters) tall,

35:32 with a dark brown complexion, and had two eyes,  two nostrils, two ears, and a small mouth.” He

35:38 said it wore “a silvery metallic suit” along  with a skullcap made from the same material.

35:43 And according to Stansel, he wasn’t  alone. Other technicians present that

35:47 day supposedly saw the same thing. And now comes the strangest part.

35:51 4. In classified government documents,

35:54 intelligence officials reportedly referred to  Arthur Stansel using the name Fritz Werner.

35:59 Those files describe how Stansel and other  technicians were allegedly transported to the

36:04 crash site aboard a bus with blacked-out windows. Then, in 2024, another document surfaced online

36:10 relating to Werner. It appeared to  contain messages exchanged between a

36:14 U.S. government official and Christopher  Mellon, the former Senate Intelligence

36:19 Committee staffer who later became involved  in the Pentagon’s investigation into UAPs.

36:24 In the exchange, the official suggested that the  truth about the Kingman crash would leave people

36:29 “slack-jawed.” He spoke about the incident  as though it remained an active matter

36:33 even into the 2020s, reportedly saying: “We’re  vacuuming up info”. That’s the kind of language

36:39 that could be interpreted as an admission  that authorities were still suppressing or

36:44 collecting information connected to the case. If genuine, the messages appeared to suggest

36:49 that a supposedly high-ranking official  believed there was at least some truth

36:54 behind Stansel’s extraordinary claims. Unfortunately, the latest tranche of

36:58 released documents doesn’t appear to add  much concrete evidence to the Kingman story.

37:02 But the allegations remind us of  something that went down in the UK.

37:06 3. After years of

37:08 sightings – and growing distrust in CIA-linked  UFO investigations – the Condon Committee was

37:13 formed. It was a project funded by the U.S.  Air Force and the University of Colorado to

37:18 scientifically study unidentified flying objects. One of the cases that got the committee’s

37:23 attention took place in 1956 at  RAF Bentwaters in Suffolk, England.

37:27 Radar operators tracked an object moving  at several thousand miles per hour. Then,

37:32 suddenly, the radar began showing dozens  of them. According to the reports,

37:36 the equipment was checked and found to be  functioning properly. Witnesses said smaller

37:40 objects appeared to dart around a much larger  one, and multiple servicemen observed the event.

37:46 Something very similar happened nearby at  RAF Lakenheath. There, the object wasn’t

37:50 only picked up on radar, it was reportedly  seen visually as well. Witnesses described

37:55 it stopping dead in the sky, accelerating  instantly, and moving at extraordinary speeds.

38:00 Lakenheath personnel contacted RAF Neatishead,  also in Suffolk, which scrambled a de Havilland

38:06 Venom night fighter to intercept the target. The Venom’s two-man crew later reported that they

38:10 had the object both on radar and in direct  visual sight. Then, without warning,

38:14 the target appeared behind them before they could  react. Eventually, the jet ran low on fuel and was

38:20 forced to break off the pursuit and land. The Condon Report would later describe the

38:23 encounter as the “most puzzling and  unusual case” it had ever examined.

38:28 So what exactly were these objects  that seemed capable of outrunning and

38:32 outmaneuvering military aircraft? Were they connected to the same

38:35 phenomena reported by American test pilots  and radar crews across the Cold War world?

38:41 2. X-15 pilot

38:43 Joseph Walker was flying at Mach 4 when he said  into the radio: “Two UFOs just passed overhead.”

38:48 They flew right past him, and were doing 3,400 mph  (5,471 kph), as fast as any plane in existence.

38:54 He said he got within about 200 feet (61 meters)  of them and saw they were disc-shaped. Walker

38:59 never got to speak about UFOs later in his life,  he died in a group formation accident in 1966.

39:06 But his words resonated with Major Robert  White, another X-15 pilot. He was traveling

39:11 at 314,000 feet (95,707 meters) when  he saw several objects flying nearby.

39:16 He told Time magazine, “There are  things out there. There absolutely are!”

39:20 This last one is important. 1.

39:23 In 2014, The Guardian posed a question: “Rather  than covering up the existence of aliens,

39:28 could it be that the real conspiracy has  been persuading us to believe in them?”

39:33 The article referred to what appeared to be  a CIA-linked psychological operation in which

39:37 fake classified UFO documents were deliberately  circulated to the public. The documents became

39:43 known as Majestic 12 papers – secret files  ostensibly proving top U.S. officials had

39:48 concealed evidence of alien contact for decades. Except the documents were exposed as forgeries.

39:54 Disinformation designed to inflame  UFO hysteria rather than calm it down.

39:59 The fallout destroyed UFO researcher, Paul  Bennewitz. After receiving supposedly leaked

40:04 information from Air Force intelligence sources,  he became convinced extraterrestrials were

40:09 operating on Earth. He later suffered  a severe psychological breakdown.

40:13 So for years, the files show us that  intelligence agencies had warned that the

40:17 American public was vulnerable to mass hysteria  surrounding UFOs. Yet there were allegations

40:23 that elements inside the national security  world had actively fueled those same fears.

40:28 Why? No one knows.

40:29 But some researchers point toward  the Psychological Strategy Board,

40:33 a Cold War-era body created to coordinate American  psychological operations and propaganda efforts.

40:39 Few ideas can capture the public imagination  more effectively than UFOs and little green men.

40:45 All the documents you’ve heard about  today are real. But as history shows,

40:49 facts and fiction have a habit of becoming  tangled, especially when governments, fear,

40:54 propaganda, and the unknown collide. The truth is out there, somewhere,

40:59 and it might be very human. Or, maybe, it’s not.

41:02 But if you’re looking for proof, it’s not  just buried in Pentagon files anymore.

41:06 It’s in close encounters, witnessed  up close by trained personnel who knew

41:11 exactly what should and shouldn’t  be in their skies. Find out what

41:14 they saw in “Actual Video Of US Military  Intercepting UFO’s”. Or watch this instead.

docs.title: YouTube Transcript: What Caused the Roman Empire to Collapse
Video Information
docs.text:
• Title: What Caused the Roman Empire to Collapse
  • Video ID: 5tilhR0C6DY
  • Published: Unknown
  • Views: Unknown
  • Language: en

docs.title: Transcript
docs.text:
00:00 The Roman Empire seemed unbeatable at  its peak - one of the largest empires

00:04 the world has ever seen. It fended off  all of its military foes. It built a

00:08 complex administrative state that ruled  regions from Egypt, to Spain, to England,

00:12 and as far east as modern-day Iraq. At its  height, it seemed like it would rule forever.

00:17 And today, it’s a distant memory.

00:20 Why did the Roman Empire ultimately fall?  Did it meet an enemy too powerful to fend

00:24 off? Was it undone by internal conflict? Or did  it simply stretch itself too thin? The answer

00:30 isn’t any one of those - and the empire’s  downfall happened over hundreds of years.

00:34 To find the truth of the Roman Empire’s fall,  we have to go back to how it became an empire

00:38 in the first place - because initially, it was a  Republic with far less territory. The Republic had

00:43 taken over from the previously flawed monarchy,  but the people seemed to be calling out for a

00:48 more unified government. One man was more than  willing to answer that call - Julius Caesar,

00:53 the man appointed perpetual dictator  of Rome in the mid-first century BCE.

00:57 He started consolidating power, becoming  a popular and effective ruler who won many

01:02 military campaigns - and many of his rivals  realized he had no intention of giving up

01:06 his newfound power. The elites of Rome  assassinated him, setting off one of the

01:10 biggest political crises in Roman history.  Civil wars kicked off as many people sought

01:15 to claim power - and in the end the wars saw  Octavian, the adopted son of Caesar, take power.

01:21 He continued his father’s legacy, conquering  nearby territories including Egypt - ending

01:26 that country’s Hellenistic era. Soon, he  was more powerful than his father ever was,

01:30 and the Roman senate responded accordingly.  They granted him the title of Augustus,

01:34 allowed him to rule in perpetuity, and soon no one  would dare challenge his power. The plotters who

01:40 feared Caesar’s role as dictator had accidentally  crafted the rise of Rome’s first Emperor.

01:46 And he wouldn’t be the last.

01:47 From then, Rome would not only become  another monarchy ruled by a series of

01:51 hereditary leaders both good and bad, but  it would develop a hunger for conquest that

01:56 would envelop a large part of Europe and  parts of Asia and Africa. While Italy would

02:00 continue to serve as the center of the  empire, the other territories would be

02:03 organized into provinces - each administered  by a local governor with drastically different

02:08 approaches to leadership. The empire would  soon be so large that it would be impossible

02:12 for one leader to maintain full control over every  territory, which meant the provinces would still

02:17 maintain some level of autonomy - as long as they  paid their taxes and didn’t cause any problems

02:22 that would arouse the ire of the Emperor.  And the system seemed to be working - the

02:26 empire was stable enough that the next two  centuries became largely known as “Pax Romana”.

02:31 But under the surface, trouble was brewing.

02:33 During the first century CE, religious conflict  started brewing under the surface. The Roman

02:38 Empire largely worshipped the traditional pantheon  - led by Jupiter and heavily tied to the Greek

02:43 pantheon led by Zeus. This polytheistic faith  was characterized by ornate temples dedicated

02:49 to the individual Gods and a wild lore that  made the Gods seem rather petty and human.

02:53 Jupiter’s dalliances with human women, and gods  taking revenge for the most petty grievances,

02:59 were both common staples of the faith in those  days - and then came Christianity. Spinning

03:04 out of the teachings of the Jewish Rabbi  known as Jesus and his eventual crucifixion

03:08 by the Roman authorities, this new Abrahamic  faith was based of the often-persecuted faith

03:13 of Judaism - and largely received the same  treatment in the early days. While some of

03:18 the more dramatic stories like early Christians  being fed to lions have no historical backing,

03:22 the Roman Empire saw new faiths  as a threat to the establishment.

03:26 But religions aren’t easy to kill.

03:28 The conflict stayed under the radar and  Christianity was mostly a small faith

03:32 during those early years, and a wise emperor  would have likely focused on maintaining the

03:36 empire’s stability rather than persecuting  heathens. But when you have a monarchy,

03:41 you’re often relying on the whims of birth  order and genetics - and in the year 177,

03:45 Rome’s luck ran out. The new Emperor, Commodus,  would soon become infamous for this exact reason.

03:51 The youngest Emperor ever at the age of  fifteen, his rule was dictated by his

03:55 emotions which led to recklessness. A teenager  making bad decisions when given too much power?

04:00 Perish the thought! As her was inheriting  the Empire built by many of his predecessors,

04:05 it was hard for him to screw up the larger things  - but back in Rome, he wasted no time throwing

04:10 things into chaos. He was known for his fickle and  dictatorial leadership style, as well as his love

04:15 of the gladiator matches in the Colosseum. He  would even participate in duels himself - which

04:19 largely meant anyone who faced off against him  would probably be expected to die quietly. He

04:24 built a cult of personality around himself,  and his reign was so chaotic that he would

04:29 eventually be immortalized by Joaquin Phoenix as  a villain in the Oscar-winning movie Gladiator.

04:33 And his reign ended as it began - with chaos.

04:37 Commodus was assassinated by a wrestler in  the Roman baths after fifteen years in charge,

04:41 and things would only get more chaotic  from there. The Roman Senate declared

04:45 him a public enemy and tore down  his statues, and he was succeeded

04:48 by a new Emperor - in what would become  known as the Year of the Five Emperors.

04:52 It was 193 CE, and civil war ensued. The next  emperor would be assassinated only three months

04:58 after taking office, his successor would  essentially pay off the guards to let him

05:01 become Emperor, and he would be ousted and  executed only weeks later. The chaos would

05:06 only die down when two emperors, Septimus Severus  and Clodius Albinus, ruled simultaneously despite

05:12 both considering the other to be a threat.  Rome’s political climate was in complete chaos.

05:17 And soon, people outside would start noticing.

05:19 Many of the provinces of Rome had been  semi-autonomous for a long time and

05:23 had developed their own cultures. So as the  Roman state spiraled into chaos, they started

05:27 to wonder - why not just make it official? As  the Romans struggled through a series of weak,

05:32 crazy, and inconsequential Emperors -  often in quick succession - territories

05:36 started to break away at an increasing rate.  First came the self-declared Gallic Empire,

05:40 which took most of the territory of  modern-day France and England with it.

05:44 Then came the Palmyrene Empire, which was led  by Queen Zenobia and took over much of Egypt

05:49 and the eastern coast of the Mediterranean -  including the many key sites in the Holy Land.

05:54 It was the biggest crisis in Rome’s history  - but it would bring many changes with it.

05:58 A series of three Emperors in the third  century would bring this crisis to the

06:02 end - but the Roman Empire that emerged from  it would not be the same. First was Aurelian,

06:06 who only reigned for five years  but had a huge impact. At the time,

06:10 the diminished Roman military was under attack  by Barbarian tribes and internal strife,

06:13 and it seemed like the Empire’s days might be  nearing an end. But Aurelian had risen through

06:18 the ranks of the military and knew its workings  well, and under his reign he fended off the

06:22 attacking tribes and conquered both the Palmyrene  Empire and the Gallic Empire. He surrounded Rome

06:27 with mighty walls, abandoned provinces that  were too much trouble to keep, and improved

06:31 Rome’s economy. Under his short tenure, Rome  started to look more like it did at its peak.

06:35 His successors would build on his work.

06:37 Diocletian would reign for twenty years and was  also a military veteran, but most of the military

06:42 work had been completed already. He would focus  his efforts on improving the empire’s stability,

06:47 which included creating a system of regional  courts that would give the empire more control

06:51 over its far-flung provinces. While the empire  had reclaimed the territory lost to the breakaway

06:56 provinces, Diocletian started expanding once  again - and by the end of his twenty years,

07:00 he became the first Roman emperor to abdicate  his position voluntarily, retiring to his palace.

07:06 But his successor might have  had an even bigger impact.

07:09 The thirty-one year run of Constantine the  Great would be among the most successful in

07:13 the empire’s history. He introduced a new  currency, expanded the empire’s territory,

07:18 and reorganized the army to be more effective.  But his most significant change was his conversion

07:23 to Christianity - reportedly spurred on by him  seeing a cross in the sky. As the Roman Emperor

07:28 converted, so did many of the citizens of Rome,  igniting Christianity’s rise to becoming a world

07:33 power religion. At the end of his reign,  the empire’s territory was near its peak,

07:36 expanding as far east as Byzantium. After his  death, Constantine left the empire to his sons,

07:41 starting a new dynasty which would rule over  Rome. The Roman Empire looked as healthy as ever,

07:46 and many people assumed that this was  the beginning of a new golden age.

07:50 So how could things go so very wrong?

07:53 The year was 337 CE when Constantine passed  away, and while Constantine’s reign had been

07:59 full of successes, there was trouble lurking  under the surface. His embrace of Christianity

08:03 had given the Church massive power in Rome, and  although many supported him in this decision,

08:08 there were some who didn’t wish for the empire to  fall under the grasps of Christianity. Enemies of

08:13 the state were executed, and their estates  were given to those he favored. The military

08:16 was paid well, but soon the soldiers seemed  to be engaging in blatant corruption. But the

08:20 empire was still the greatest power in the world,  and it was hard to imagine anyone challenging it.

08:24 But empire’s aren’t immune from internal strife.

08:27 In the aftermath of the death of Constantine,  the throne of the empire was once again open

08:31 for contest, and this era led to many conflicts  over who would take control. His sons initially

08:36 ruled jointly, but chaos would follow and  Rome would be plunged into civil war. Many

08:41 territories were taken over by local leaders,  with territories going back and forth at the

08:45 whims of military victories. Despite this,  the core of the empire was unchallenged,

08:49 and by 379 a new emperor named Theodosius had  risen. A proven general, he would become one

08:55 of Rome’s greatest military leaders and  would put an end to this era of strife.

08:58 But far greater threats were  brewing beyond the borders of Rome.

09:02 As far-reaching as Rome’s borders were at the  time, it was hard to believe that a nomadic people

09:07 from a continent away would throw the whole thing  into chaos. But the Huns were no ordinary nomads.

09:12 Fierce warriors, they had been making inroads into  Asia and Eastern Europe - and where they went,

09:17 people fled. Their mass takeover of territory led  the local Gothic tribes to flee towards the Roman

09:23 Empire. Suddenly, the Romans had a huge influx  of barbarian warriors fleeing across their border

09:27 - and Rome’s lack of management in their border  states came back to haunt them. A well-organized

09:32 government may have been able to resettle these  new residents and incorporate them into the

09:36 Roman state - even using their warrior smarts  to reinvigorate the military. Unfortunately,

09:41 the corrupt local officials instead chose to  exploit them, assuming they weren’t a threat.

09:45 They would be proven very wrong.

09:47 Now the Romans had a large number of outside  warriors within their borders. These guests

09:52 had seen Roman hospitality was lacking, and  they quickly took up arms. They were joined

09:56 by other tribesmen heading over the  border, and what started as a refugee

10:00 crisis quickly turned into a guerilla war. While  Rome had a superior military force, it was also

10:05 spread out and concentrated in the cities, and the  forces that were sent to confront the Goths found

10:10 the invaders fought much harder than expected. The  elites felt very little of this crisis - they were

10:15 kept safe in their walled cities - but across  the massive expanses of the Roman countryside,

10:19 the Goths quickly gained territory and claimed the  land of former Roman subjects across the Balkans.

10:24 And Theodosius may have neglected  this problem a bit too much.

10:28 The Emperor may have restored Rome’s  military in some ways, but the coffers

10:32 were still looking kind of bare after decades  of patronage under his predecessors. He raised

10:37 taxes to confront the barbarians - and was met  with rebellions from the people he ruled over.

10:41 He also cracked down on other faiths, doubling  down on Constantine’s embrace of Christianity,

10:45 and even persecuted believers of other  variants of Christianity. Soon he was

10:49 facing new rebellions in the west seeking to  end his rule, with rebel leader Magnus Maximus

10:54 declaring himself emperor in 383 and taking over  the territory of Gaul. This led to significant

11:00 losses in territory and troops until Maximus  made a failed attempt at defeating Rome itself

11:05 and was ultimately defeated in 388. Rome once  again became the greatest power on the planet.

11:10 But soon this would all change.

11:12 By 395 CE, Theodosius I would die, leaving behind  him a weakened army and no clear successor. His

11:19 two sons would each claim the empire, but neither  was a capable leader - leaving their ministers to

11:23 essentially take charge of the situation. Rather  than go to another brutal civil war only a decade

11:28 after the last, the two halves of the empire  essentially went their own separate ways - one

11:32 emperor, Arcadius, took the eastern Roman Empire,  which would become known as the Byzantine Empire

11:37 in the future, while the other son, Honorius,  would take the western part including Rome itself.

11:42 It was the biggest loss of territory for Rome yet  - and this time, there would be no going back.

11:47 The Byzantine Empire would endure, lasting  for another thousand years with a power

11:51 base in the city of Constantinople - but  it would never reach the world-defining

11:55 power of the Roman Empire. As for Rome, it  still ruled much of Europe - but its days

12:00 were drawing short. Without the massive  territory now owned by the Byzantines,

12:04 administering the empire was much more  manageable - but it also meant the massive

12:08 barbarian invasions were harder to control. The  leader of the Huns, Attila, was one of the most

12:13 feared military leaders of all time - and now  he placed his full attention on taking Rome.

12:18 It would be a death of a thousand  cuts for the Roman Empire.

12:21 Over the next eighty years, the Roman Empire dealt  with brutal attacks from the Huns on their fringes

12:26 and the Gothic population throughout the empire.  The Roman military was a shadow of what it used

12:30 to be, and it frequently found itself in retreat.  The territory of the empire shrunk piece by piece,

12:35 and Rome started to look less like a powerful  empire and more like a city in decline. Some

12:40 leaders would manage to restore the military’s  strength, but none would get it back to the level

12:43 where it could reclaim significant amounts of  territory. The empire would limp along until 476,

12:49 where one ambitious king decided it  was time to strike the final blow.

12:53 His name was Odoacer - and the  mostly-forgotten figure may have

12:56 been one of the most important people in history.

12:58 The last Emperor of Rome, Romulus  Augustulus, had a mighty name but

13:04 was only a sixteen year old boy when Odoacer  invaded. The barbarian king, surprisingly,

13:09 dealt kindly with the young king as he sacked  Rome - accepting his surrender and allowing the

13:13 boy to remain alive. He sent him away to live  with relatives, even granting him a pension,

13:17 before declaring himself the ruler of Italy.  Probably the most dramatic firing from a first

13:22 job a teenager had ever experienced! But now, the  Roman Empire was over - or was it? That depends on

13:28 how you define it, because Odoacer now ruled what  was left of it - but he was considered a foreign

13:32 occupier. The Roman Senate didn’t consider him a  legitimate Roman ruler and instead transferred the

13:37 seal of Rome to the eastern empire. And so the  greatest empire in history passed into legend.

13:42 Or did it?

13:43 The Roman empire as a government was no more,  but its greatest institution still remained - the

13:48 Roman Catholic Church. It was still in its  infancy, less than five hundred years old,

13:51 but its faith had spread very quickly and would  soon grow its roots in most of Europe. As the

13:56 Church spread, so did its power - and for  the best part of the next thousand years,

14:00 it would be the de facto government in much  of Europe. Even kings would answer to it,

14:04 and few would challenge the Pope’s  power until Henry VIII would start

14:08 his own religion when the Church  wouldn’t let him get divorced. So,

14:11 while the Roman Empire did not control Europe  anymore, the Church’s legacy far outlive it.

14:16 But why did the empire actually fall?

14:18 There is no one reason why the Roman Empire  crumbled, but many factors played a role - few

14:23 bigger than the collapse of its military. Rome’s  army was once the most powerful in the world,

14:27 and it attracted the best with good pay. But as  the empire’s coffers declined, it soon struggled

14:32 to recruit new troops effectively. This led  to Emperors filing out the ranks with foreign

14:36 mercenaries, who neither had the skills nor the  loyalty of previous armies. Many even came from

14:41 the invading armies they were fighting, and the  effectiveness of their fighting forces suffered.

14:45 They tried to make up for the personnel  problem - but that just made things worse.

14:49 Many emperors consistently overspent on  the military, but that didn’t make it any

14:53 easier to manage. The huge territory they  had to govern made it near impossible to

14:57 communicate effectively, and with no e-mail  or teams groups to share important memos,

15:01 it was often a matter of weeks or months before  key changes in policy were communicated. As the

15:06 empire got larger and larger, this became a  bigger problem - and soon the empire was more

15:10 focused on protecting its key cities than  effectively managing its whole territory.

15:14 But inside Rome itself, things  weren’t doing much better.

15:17 One of the biggest problems with Rome in its last  days was the lack of strong leadership - right up

15:22 to the top. Being Roman Emperor was not a  great job. Given that it was an appointed

15:26 position that came with near-unlimited power,  a lot of people wanted it - and that meant that

15:31 getting the job came with massive risks. At one  point between the second and third centuries,

15:35 over twenty men held the title in less than  75 years - and the most common way to be fired

15:40 from this job was with a knife between  your ribs. Turns out Julius Caesar was a

15:44 trendsetter. When an Emperor did manage  to hold onto power for years, there was

15:48 a good chance they would essentially turn the  empire into their own personal patronage mill,

15:52 appointing their allies to powerful positions. And  the Emperor’s bodyguards, the Praetorian Guard,

15:57 would often take matters into their own hands and  assassinate emperors when they became more trouble

16:02 than they were worth. With a government like this,  is it any wonder that the empire began crumbling?

16:06 All of these factors came together,  spelling the end of the Roman Empire.

16:09 For centuries, the Roman Empire had  been unchallenged on a military level.

16:13 Their expeditions would face little to no  opposition, and their army could largely

16:17 sweep into a territory and take it over as  they pleased. Conquering new territories often

16:21 meant having to build new infrastructure that  would increase quality of life in the region

16:25 in some way as well as enforcing the rule  of the Roman Empire on its newly acquired

16:29 citizens. So the army wound up being more of  an enforcement arm of the Roman government,

16:33 and it was no longer prepared to deal with  major military conflict. So when outsiders

16:37 such as the Goths came calling after being  pushed out of their territory by the Huns,

16:41 the Roman military wasn’t forimdable  enough to maintain its borders.

16:44 And it all came down to one fatal mistake.

16:47 If the military was well-prepared for this  invasion, the odds are they could have defeated

16:51 the Goth armies and defended their territory. They  were better trained and had superior weaponry than

16:55 the Goths. But once the Goths had managed to  enter the fringes of the empire, it was going to

16:59 be much harder to displace them without a major  military operation. The Romans ultimately chose

17:05 the worst option of all - they didn’t aggressively  repel the Goth invaders and defend their borders,

17:09 but they also didn’t welcome them into the empire  and take advantage of this new manpower like they

17:14 could have. Instead, they exploited them and hired  them while never letting them develop any loyalty

17:19 to the empire. This led to constant civil wars  and small military skirmishes, growing tension,

17:24 and a slow but sure loss of territory. And  it all could have been avoided if the Empire

17:29 coordinate a better response to the Goths seeking  refuge within the borders of the Roman Empire.

17:33 Want to learn more about the end  of empires? Watch “Real Reason

17:36 Ancient Egyptians Went Extinct”,  or check out this video instead.

docs.title: YouTube Transcript: 16 Most Disturbing Videos From Pentagon UFO Release
Video Information
docs.text:
• Title: 16 Most Disturbing Videos From Pentagon UFO Release
  • Video ID: 6dPNiN5nf0E
  • Published: Unknown
  • Views: Unknown
  • Language: en

docs.title: Transcript
docs.text:
00:00 The Pentagon just dropped its first UFO files and  it includes over 160 documents and never before

00:06 seen videos of unexplained aerial phenomena…  And some of the footage genuinely looks hard

00:11 to explain 16.

00:14 We’ll begin with one of the  shortest clips in the entire batch,

00:17 lasting just 5 seconds. Blink and you’ll  miss a dark, cigar-shaped object shooting

00:22 across the frame from the left to right. According to the Pentagon’s description,

00:26 this video was captured by an infrared sensor  aboard a U.S. military platform in May, 2022.

00:32 It was submitted to the All-domain Anomaly  Resolution Office (AARO) by U.S. Central

00:37 Command, with a report suggesting  it could be a “possible missile.”

00:41 When the footage is slowed down, that  explanation actually starts to make sense.

00:45 The shape is long and narrow, closely matching  a missile, especially as it was filmed over the

00:50 Middle East. At the same time, UFO supporters  point out that the military doesn’t usually

00:55 submit footage like this to AARO unless there’s  at least some uncertainty about what it is.

01:00 In other words, the fact it was  even flagged suggests it wasn’t

01:04 immediately and confidently identified. So, there’s a chance it could have been

01:08 something else.. 15.

01:10 The next video lasts just over a minute in total. It was also captured by US Central Command at some

01:16 point in 2020 and shared with the AARO. It’s worth noting the original reporter

01:21 made an edit, pausing the footage at the  10-second mark. They also added a note

01:26 highlighting a “small thermal signature” near  the top of the frame, shown as a white orb.

01:31 Beyond that, no other changes  were made to the footage.

01:34 After the pause, the video follows the orb as  it seems to weave from side to side through

01:38 the sky at a relatively slow speed. At times, it  disappears behind redacted sections of the frame,

01:44 and the operator cycles through different contrast  and zoom settings. Despite this, no clear details

01:49 ever actually emerge. The object just looks like  a small sphere of light, with no distinctive

01:54 features or characteristics whatsoever. Many of the videos in the UFO files are

01:59 similar to this one, captured on cameras that  weren’t designed for high-resolution recording.

02:03 On the one hand, those who believe in aliens  could argue that this may very well be some

02:08 sort of craft from another galaxy, due to  its unusual movements and unclear shape. But

02:13 skeptics just as easily point out that this  UAP could be anything from a weather balloon

02:18 to a random piece of airborne debris, like a  wedding lantern drifting away on the breeze.

02:24 14. Many of the declassified

02:26 videos take place above bodies of water, just like  PR29. This was captured over the Gulf of Oman in

02:32 2024 and submitted to AARO by US Northern Command. It’s a short clip at just 21 seconds. But it comes

02:39 with a separate mission report describing “an  object with a vertical pole or bar attached to

02:45 the bottom” that seemed to be skimming  just above the surface of the water.

02:49 The person submitting the report also suggests  that the UAP might actually be a reflection of

02:53 something moving beneath the water’s surface.  That would explain its speed and behavior.

02:58 The Pentagon itself describes the anomaly  as an “inverted teardrop” that stays mostly

03:03 centered in the sensor’s field of view  throughout the clip. It moves in a clean,

03:07 straight line across the frame, with a clear  rod-like extension sticking out from its base.

03:12 UFO enthusiasts argue that this could be an  example of a so-called ‘jellyfish UFO. There

03:17 have been other sightings of this type  of unidentified aircraft in the past.

03:21 But naysayers think it’s more likely some sort  of balloon, or even a bunch of balloons tied

03:26 together. They add that the object only  seems to be going so fast because of the

03:30 way that the video was filmed, creating a  well-documented visual phenomenon called

03:34 the ‘parallax effect,’ which can distort  the way we see and interpret moving images.

03:39 What do you think? 13.

03:41 The next video was captured in North America  and was submitted by the Department of the Army.

03:45 It’s almost 2 minutes in length and is one of the  most recent files, having been captured in 2026.

03:51 The opening frames show a camera locked onto  some sort of object, which seems to be a drone.

03:56 Suddenly, a white heat signature darts across  the screen from the right side to the left.

04:01 The camera quickly readjusts,  trying to track the anomaly,

04:04 adjusting its field of view in the process. At this point, two distinct heat-like spheres

04:09 come into view, apparently connected to a single  body as they move together in sync. For nearly

04:14 2 minutes, the camera tracks the anomaly,  zooming in and out, making the spheres appear

04:18 to shift in size as the perspective changes. Analysts studying the footage have noticed what

04:23 seems to be some sort of exhaust plume trailing  behind the object. That may hint at the true

04:28 identity of the anomaly. Experts  argue that it’s some sort of plane,

04:32 leaving a visible trail behind. The next video, however, isn’t quite

04:36 as conclusive. 12.

04:38 At more than 5 minutes in length, PR44  is longer than most of the other videos

04:43 released by the Pentagon. It was filed by the US

04:46 Central Command and captured in 2020 in an  undisclosed location in the Arabian Gulf.

04:51 While there’s no oral or written description  of this incident, the Pentagon has provided a

04:55 detailed commentary. The first 30 seconds  are pretty uneventful, but after that,

04:59 an unidentified object appears. The camera  then tracks the anomaly for around 3 minutes,

05:04 keeping it generally in the center of the frame  while adjusting both contrast and zoom levels.

05:09 Eventually, the camera stops tracking  the UAP, which then leaves the frame.

05:13 The length of this video has drawn attention,  with some analysts arguing it wouldn’t have been

05:18 tracked that long unless the operator thought  it was genuinely unusual or worth monitoring.

05:24 Others point out that even with zoom and contrast  adjustments, the footage never really sharpens.

05:29 It just remains a vague white orb, leaving plenty  of room for more mundane explanations like a drone

05:34 or balloon. 11.

05:37 Next, let’s take a look at what the Pentagon  has labeled PR36. It’s another unresolved

05:42 UAP captured by an infrared sensor  aboard a US military platform at some

05:47 point in 2020, somewhere in the Middle East. The video was accompanied by a written report,

05:51 which mentioned a “solid white object  making erratic movements above the water.”

05:56 The footage is heavily redacted, with large  black boxes obscuring much of the on-screen

06:00 action. However, we can still make out some  sort of anomaly entering the frame from the

06:04 left side after 5 seconds. The object looks like a

06:08 small white egg-shaped orb. The operator shifts between

06:11 camera settings and seems to lose sight of the  object for a moment, before locking back onto it.

06:16 For nearly 2 minutes, the UAP drifts through  the sky while the camera struggles to keep

06:21 it centered. Its speed and direction are  hard to pin down, since the operator is

06:25 constantly panning and adjusting to follow it. As the clip goes on, the operator zooms in,

06:30 making the object appear larger until it drifts  out of the top of the frame and the video ends.

06:35 UFO researchers say its shape is unusual,  with no clear wings, fins, or visible

06:40 propulsion. There’s nothing that matches the  characteristics of a conventional aircraft.

06:45 Skeptics, though, note there’s a long list of  possibilities, from balloons and lanterns to

06:50 satellites, drones, and other airborne objects  that can easily look unfamiliar on camera.

06:55 10.

06:56 File PR26 was recorded in October 2023,  somewhere around the United Arab Emirates.

07:02 It consists of 43 seconds of footage, with  a separate PDF file confirming that a UAP

07:08 of some description was spotted during a mission. The clip shows a small white mass speeding toward

07:13 the left side of the frame as the camera  struggles to keep up with it. Eventually,

07:17 the camera stops tracking the object,  which darts off out of the picture.

07:21 Analysts have slowed the footage down  and zoomed in to get a better look.

07:25 Some describe it as a mass of orbs. Others  note that it has a bird-like appearance,

07:30 with clear wing-like features and even a tail,  which becomes particularly clear when zoomed in.

07:35 As a result, opinions on this  particular clip are mixed.

07:38 Some say that it most likely was a bird or even  a fixed-wing drone. Others say it could have been

07:43 some sort of advanced, aerodynamically designed  alien craft, attempting to evade detection.

07:49 9. Next, another

07:51 very brief clip with another of those ‘blink and  you’ll miss it’ moments, but still one that the US

07:56 military felt was interesting enough to share. The clip itself, labeled PR31 and captured in

08:01 Syria in 2024, shows an aerial view of some  sort of structure, which could be a residence

08:07 or even potentially a military building. The video is only 5 seconds in length,

08:11 and it’s the first second that actually  matters. It shows a strange visual anomaly

08:16 darting erratically across the top of the  screen, before disappearing from view.

08:20 The anomaly is described by the Pentagon as  “multicolored,” though the original reporter

08:25 claimed it was more of a “misshapen  and uneven ball of white light.” They

08:29 added that a kind of “light/glare halo  effect” was produced as it passed by.

08:33 Skeptics have been quick to write this video off  as little more than lens flare. That might be the

08:38 most logical explanation of what happened here. At the same time, people argue that lens flares

08:43 usually have a more predictable pattern  of movement. This one, however, seems to

08:47 move up and down before it leaves the frame,  which could suggest that there's more to it.

08:51 Interestingly, the incident was also captured in  two more of the videos released by the Pentagon,

08:55 files PR32 and PR33. They both show the  same object but from different angles.

09:02 In video PR32, we also see a strange  flare-like phenomenon, with a curved,

09:07 almost halo-like beam of light at the  top of the video before fading from view.

09:11 PR33, meanwhile, shows the anomaly from above. For a split second, two irregular orange shapes

09:17 flash over the background,  then vanish just as quickly.

09:20 It might be easy enough for skeptics to explain  away one visual anomaly. But three separate visual

09:26 phenomena captured on three separate cameras  all at the exact same moment is slightly harder

09:31 to explain. Some UFO fans argued that this could  have been some sort of ultra-fast craft speeding

09:37 through the area. 8.

09:39 Another of the videos that has sparked debate  online is file PR35, which relates to an

09:44 unresolved UAP report from Greece in October 2023. An accompanying mission report described the sight

09:50 of a “small and circular” UAP that was  flying close to the surface of the ocean.

09:55 We see the unidentified object just a couple  of seconds into the video as it speeds along,

10:00 seemingly in a straight line. It’s worth  noting that the view here is from above,

10:04 looking down onto the sea. There are  other objects that come into frame,

10:08 which may be boats or other kinds of crafts. The anomaly, however, appears to be moving far

10:13 too fast to be any sort of naval vessel. It moves quickly toward the coastline,

10:17 but as the view shifts from water to  land, it becomes impossible to track.

10:21 Several other clips in the files show objects  that suddenly fade or disappear mid-frame,

10:26 almost as if they just drop out of view.  Again,the grainy footage fails to give any

10:30 clear details of the anomaly in question. So it’s  difficult to know exactly what we’re seeing here.

10:34 Skeptics argue that this could be any number  of man-made items. UFO enthusiasts point to

10:40 its rapid rate of travel, plus the strange way  it disappears from view, as evidence to support

10:45 their arguments that it might be something more. Many have also noted how this object is first

10:49 seen over water, which is also the case for many  of the other anomalies caught on camera in the

10:54 other files. 7.

10:56 Another mysterious object can be seen in video  PR28, which was reportedly captured over Greece

11:02 in January 2024. It’s a relatively short video,  but quite interesting, for a number of reasons.

11:08 For starters, the video was accompanied by a  separate mission report file which described

11:12 seeing some sort of “diamond-shaped” entity. They  added that it was moving at a speed of 434 knots,

11:18 or 500 miles per hour (804 kph). Perhaps the most interesting part

11:21 was that the object was only detectable  via a short-wave infrared (SWIR) sensor.

11:26 In the first 10 seconds, the screen is split  between electro-optical and SWIR views.

11:31 A faint area of contrast then appears near  the center of the split frame. It quickly

11:36 switches to full-screen SWIR, revealing an  “inverted teardrop” shape with a “vertically

11:41 linear trailing mass” hanging below it. Just before the minute mark of the video,

11:46 the operator tries to shift  to a visible spectrum view,

11:49 but the object vanishes. When they transition back  to SWIR, they are unable to locate the object.

11:54 It literally vanishes in mid-air. Some commentators have argued that this object

11:58 could be some sort of cluster of balloons, but  there are a couple of clear flaws in that theory.

12:03 Firstly, the report notes that this  object was moving extremely fast.

12:07 Second, the fact that it only showed  up on the SWIR screen suggests that

12:10 it wasn’t a normal physical object that  could easily be seen with the naked eye.

12:14 UFO enthusiasts argue it could be another  example of a ‘jellyfish’ style spacecraft.

12:20 Next, the one video that gives us arguably the  clearest look at a potential ‘flying saucer.’

12:25 6. Only 2 of the videos released

12:28 in the UFO files are listed as having taken  place in North America, and PR45 is one of them.

12:33 This particular video was reportedly  captured in the Southern United States,

12:37 home to a lot of famous US sightings in  places like Texas, Georgia, and Florida.

12:42 This video was submitted by the Department of  the Air Force and is just under a minute long.

12:46 It was captured in 2020 and shows a  targeting reticle locking onto what

12:50 first appears to be a ball of light, similar  to the objects the other clips seen so far.

12:55 The sensor narrows its field of view, zooming  in on the area of contrast to give us a

13:00 clearer look as it grows in size and detail. The most fascinating moment comes at the end,

13:05 when the small white dot suddenly appears  much larger, almost like the classic “flying

13:10 saucer” from older sci-fi films. AARO notes this change in size is

13:15 most likely just perspective, as the  US platform gets closer to the object.

13:19 In either case, the shape we see before  the anomaly exits the frame is strange.

13:24 It doesn’t appear to resemble any  known aircraft and has invited a lot

13:28 of speculation and discussion online  about what this object actually is.

13:32 5. Most of

13:33 the Pentagon’s UFO files show little more than  small white orbs or vague shapes moving across

13:39 the frame at speed. In many cases, they could  just as easily be drones, birds, or balloons.

13:44 This one, however, is a little different. File PR47 was submitted by the US

13:49 Indo-Pacific Command and captured  in 2023 somewhere around Japan.

13:53 It lasts for almost 2 minutes, and while not  much happens in the clip, it’s still triggered

13:58 plenty of discussion online. It’s all down to  the strange nature of the anomaly involved.

14:03 The Pentagon describes it as being made  up of “three distinct areas of contrast”

14:07 which “appear to maintain a fixed position  and orientation relative to one another.”

14:12 The video begins with a  vague shape in the distance.

14:15 A few seconds later, the camera zooms in and  the full nature of the anomaly is revealed:

14:20 what seemed to be one shape actually  appears to be three distinct rings

14:24 of light that seem to be connected. As the Pentagon’s description states, the

14:28 shapes maintain a fixed position and orientation  to one another, meaning that they all move as one,

14:34 and the camera tracks the anomaly for some  time before the video comes to a sudden end.

14:38 While skeptics have been able to explain most  of the videos, there hasn’t been any clear,

14:42 conclusive explanation for this one. Some say the rings might just be some

14:46 sort of visual distortion caused by lights on  an aircraft or a drone. But those who believe

14:51 in extraterrestrials argue that the appearance of  this anomaly is one of the best pieces of evidence

14:56 for alien life in the entire batch of files. And, as the next video proves, this wasn’t

15:01 the only example of a strangely shaped  object that left viewers mystified.

15:06 4. The next video was also captured and

15:08 submitted by the US Indo-Pacific Command, this  time in the East China Sea, sometime in 2024.

15:14 It’s one of the shorter clips in  the set, lasting just 10 seconds.

15:18 Again, it revolves around an anomalous  entity that doesn’t really move around

15:21 during the video itself but has a very bizarre  appearance. One that analysts have struggled

15:26 to come up with a rational explanation for. The Pentagon describes this anomaly as “a

15:30 football-shaped body with three radial  projections: one oriented vertically,

15:35 and two oriented downward at a 45-degree angle  relative to the major axis of the main mass.”

15:41 There does appear to be a larger central mass,  with two protrusions extending from the base

15:46 and another rising vertically from the rear. Analysts noted that the anomaly almost seems

15:51 to be pulsing, with wave-like movements. Some  have even described it as ‘organic’ in nature.

15:57 They believe it could be some sort of  gravity-bending spacecraft, turning the laws

16:00 of physics upside down with its very existence. From a more skeptical perspective, this could

16:05 just be a small aircraft or drone filmed  at an awkward angle. It would naturally

16:10 distort its shape and make it look unusual.  In that case, the “radial projections” are

16:14 probably just wings or stabilising fins,  rather than anything unusual or unknown.

16:19 As with the rest of the videos, there’s no way to  be entirely sure on what this anomaly actually is.

16:24 That's what makes it an ‘anomaly’. But  it’s one of the stranger-looking entities

16:29 captured on camera and shared with the public. CBS News Pentagon reporter Eleanor Watson even

16:34 included this clip in her personal list of the  six most interesting videos of the entire file

16:39 release. 3.

16:40 File PR34 was captured by a US military  platform in 2023, somewhere around

16:45 Greece. It was submitted to AARO by US Central  Command, along with a detailed mission report.

16:51 In that report, an unidentified object  is described as traveling at speeds of

16:55 “approximately 80 miles per hour” (129  kph) close to the surface of the ocean,

16:58 while “making multiple 90-degree turns.” Some of the internet’s biggest UAP and UFO experts

17:04 and analysts have called this one of, if not the  most impressive videos in the entire set of files.

17:10 It’s not hard to see why. It runs for almost three minutes,

17:13 and things kick off right away as a small  object appears in the bottom-left of the frame.

17:18 It then snaps into a sharp 90-degree turn,  darting left while still moving at high speed.

17:23 It then appears to come to a sudden  stop before turning back on itself.

17:27 In the seconds that follow, we see the object  continue to move across the screen, going left

17:31 then right and up and down. It continuously stops  and readjusts its flight path in unexpected ways.

17:37 The camera locks onto the object, which  then stops its erratic movement and

17:41 continues in a straight line for a while  before suddenly disappearing from view.

17:44 Skeptics suggest the sharp turns, sudden  directional changes and consistent speed

17:49 could indicate a drone. Others, however, say  that the object’s behavior, combined with the

17:54 way it seems to vanish in mid-air, suggest  that it could be something otherworldly.

17:59 Next, let’s talk about a video that a former  US Navy Admiral called “absolutely remarkable.”

18:04 2. PR48 is a 1 minute

18:07 and 39-second clip captured by an infrared sensor  on board a US military platform. It was recorded

18:13 at some point in 2024, at what seems to be a  wind farm, somewhere in the Indo-Pacific region.

18:18 The Pentagon’s description for this video  is quite brief, noting the appearance of

18:22 an “area of contrast,” far from the camera  that shows up as a faint glowing white orb.

18:28 What stands out here isn’t how  it looks… but how it moves.

18:31 The tiny orb flies through the wind farm,  weaving between the turbines at what seems

18:35 to be a high speed. Eventually it reaches  the end and then turns back on itself.

18:39 Former Rear Admiral Timothy Gallaudet  told reporters that this video “can’t be

18:43 explained,” but that hasn’t stopped online  analysts from attempting to unpack it.

18:48 Those on the skeptic side argued that  the object could easily be a drone,

18:51 and the internet is littered with examples of  people piloting their drones through wind farms.

18:56 However, analysts quickly countered that  argument. They point out that turbines or

19:00 windmills in offshore wind farms typically  have to be spaced at least several hundred

19:04 feet apart from one another. This object passes  from one turbine to the next at great speeds.

19:09 Some have estimated that it may even be  moving faster than the speed of sound,

19:13 which would be far beyond the  capacities of any commercial drone.

19:16 So, what’s the real explanation here? Well, some analysts have dug deeper

19:20 into the video, stabilizing it  and analyzing it frame by frame.

19:24 They claim the speed and erratic movement  are most likely an optical illusion caused

19:28 by how the footage was recorded. In their  opinion the object is actually travelling

19:32 in a fairly straight line and sits much farther  away from the turbines than it actually appears.

19:38 1. Now we come

19:40 to one of the strangest video of the entire batch  and the one that stands out the most: file PR38.

19:46 It was reportedly captured by  an infrared sensor back in 2013.

19:50 No oral or written description was provided,  but the Pentagon has added its own summary

19:55 of the scene. It describes how something  resembling “an eight-pointed star with arms

19:59 of alternating length” appears on the screen  early into the almost 2-minute-long video.

20:04 As the clip progresses, the strange star shape  moves in unusual patterns across the screen. At

20:10 times, it seems to slowly drift one way before  suddenly taking a sharp turn in a different

20:15 direction. The Pentagon’s report also notes that  the shape appears to have its own visible trail.

20:20 Halfway through the video, a second, much larger  shape appears on screen. It drifts in and out of

20:25 view a couple of times before disappearing. Soon after, the eight-pointed star eventually

20:29 speeds off the top of the  frame before the video ends.

20:32 This video generated a lot of excitement and  debate online following the files’ release.

20:37 Some viewers were understandably disturbed by  the sight of such a strange shape that appears

20:41 to move around in unnatural patterns. However, eagle-eyed analysts soon came

20:45 up with a logical explanation for the entire  video. According to them, what we’re seeing

20:50 isn’t an advanced alien spacecraft, but  a parachute flare used in conflict zones.

20:55 The flares are launched into the air and drift  down slowly under small parachutes. Because they

21:00 burn extremely hot, infrared cameras often  distort them into “starburst” shapes due to

21:05 thermal blooming, which matches what we see in  the footage. This could also explain the second

21:09 object, which looks just like a parachute. Due to the flares being lightweight,

21:13 they’re easily affected by the  wind. That would also explain why

21:16 the star seems veer around in random directions. As with the other clips, there might be a rational

21:22 explanation, but there’s just enough ambiguity  to keep people questioning what they’re seeing.

21:27 It leaves the bigger question hanging: are  we truly alone in a vast, empty universe,

21:31 or is there something else out there? The next release of files may

21:35 bring more answers… or more questions. And if these sightings already seem unsettling,

21:40 some of the most disturbing encounters of all  involve highly classified sites. Find out more in

21:45 ‘Military Can’t Explain These UFOs at US & Russian  Nuclear Weapons Sites.’ Or watch this instead.
