00:00 The inside job that helped Hitler rise to power.  A huge coverup of the most horrifying moment of

00:05 the Vietnam War. And a secret CIA weapon that  could kill you without ever leaving a trace.

00:11 They sound crazy, but these are just some  of the most insane conspiracy theories

00:14 that turned out to be completely true! And  we’re going to let you in on all the secrets.

00:19 My Lai Massacre Cover Up. Sadly, there is no shortage

00:22 of atrocities committed during the Vietnam  War, but there is one so awful and so damning

00:27 to the United States that the truth about it was  intentionally hidden from the public. The My Lai

00:32 Massacre took place in the small Vietnam hamlet  of My Lai, on March 16th, 1968. That morning,

00:38 US soldiers entered the village on a search and  destroy mission. While the region where My Lai

00:43 was situated was controlled by Viet Cong guerilla  fighters, the American troops found no sign of

00:48 enemy combatants in the area, only civilians. That didn’t stop the United States own soldiers

00:53 from setting huts on fire, murdering between 347  to 504 innocent Vietnamese people – including

01:00 as many as fifty children under the age of four  – and committing acts of assault so deplorable

01:05 against the women of My Lai that we can’t actually  describe them here on YouTube. Even worse, the

01:10 barbaric actions of these troops were initially  praised by the US as fabricated reports claimed

01:15 that over a hundred and twenty of these needlessly  murdered civilians had actually been Viet Cong.The

01:20 truth about the My Lai Massacre wouldn’t emerge  until a year later, and became emblematic of the

01:25 US’ war efforts in Vietnam. The conflict had  already been widely criticised and protested,

01:31 and now it looked like America had lost any  sense of morality when it came to the actions

01:35 of its troops in Southeast Asia. Military secrecy  around the killings ultimately made it all the

01:40 more shocking when the revelations were made  public when former soldiers spoke out about

01:45 it. These weren’t just crimes against humanity  perpetrated against innocent women and children

01:50 by American troops, but acts that the US Army  leadership had conspired to sweep under the rug.

01:56 Among the slew of court martials that followed,  Lieutenant William Calley was accused of directing

02:00 the My Lai Massacre, and as a result was convicted  of premeditated murder and sentenced to life

02:06 behind bars. Sickeningly, he only served  three and a half years of house arrest,

02:10 before having his sentence commuted… at  the behest of then-President Richard Nixon.

02:15 But if you think that’s crazy, it’s nothing  compared to the true conspiratorial weirdness

02:19 that came out in the Church Committee Findings. Named for the US Senator at the helm, Frank Church

02:24 was the chair of the Senate Select Committee to  Study Governmental Operations with Respect to

02:29 Intelligence Activities. This was a 1975 Senate  investigation into alleged illegal activity

02:35 carried out by the US’ own intelligence agencies,  including the Federal Bureau of Investigation,

02:40 the Central Intelligence Agency,  and the National Security Agency.

02:44 Church Committee findings included multiple  attempted assassinations of other countries’

02:49 political figureheads, including President Fidel  Castro of Cuba, as well as the presidents of the

02:54 Dominican Republic and the Democratic Republic  of the Congo. There was COINTELPRO, a covert

02:59 operation conducted by the FBI to infiltrate  specific domestic organizations like civil

03:05 rights activists, feminists, environmentalists,  people protesting the Vietnam War, and communists.

03:11 It considered these groups ‘subversive’,  and sought to discredit them.

03:15 The Church Committee also brought to light Project  Mockingbird, an effort by the CIA to leverage

03:20 its relationships with journalists to control the  flow of information in the news. Project MINARET,

03:25 wherein the NSA was working with telecommunication  companies to monitor individuals on a watch

03:30 list – a list that included Senator Church  and other members of the Church Committee.

03:34 And, were it not for the work of the Church  Committee, the world might never have learned

03:38 about the horrendous CIA experiments that took  place as part of Projects MKULTRA and MKNAOMI.

03:44 But these weren’t even the strangest  findings of the committee… stay tuned

03:48 to hear about the CIA’s secret weapon. The findings made by the Church Committee,

03:52 as horrifying as they were, led to important  reforms when it came to how US intelligence

03:56 agencies operate. Congressional committees were  to oversee the future activities of the FBI,

04:01 CIA and NSA, and famously President Gerald Ford  issued Executive Order 11905, which banned the

04:08 carrying out of political assassinations. Let’s head back to Europe, though,

04:12 and peer into the dark plot that helped install  one of history’s greatest monsters: This is

04:17 the Reichstag Fire and the Nazi Power Grab. There’s no denying that the Nazi Party went

04:22 about assuming power over Germany in the most  brutal way possible during the early thirties.

04:27 On February 27, 1933, the Reichstag, which  was used as the home of Germany’s Parliament,

04:32 was burned to the ground. The attacks were  initially blamed on communists, with Dutchman

04:37 Marinus van der Lubbe playing the role of pasty. Thanks to van der Lubbe being a communist, Adolf

04:42 Hitler – already Chancellor at this time – used  the fire as justification for forcibly expelling

04:47 any left leaning or communist politicians out  of Parliament, and had them imprisoned so they

04:53 couldn’t oppose the Nazi Party in the elections  that took place a month later in March 1933.

04:58 Hitler successfully turned Germany against  communists by declaring that they were

05:02 threatening to take over, thus allowing the Nazis  to win more seats in the elections and helping

05:07 them to assume power over the country. It's hardly a stretch to conclude that

05:10 the Nazis were responsible, especially  given how partial they were for burning

05:14 books and attacking other institutions  that challenged their fascist ideology.

05:19 Operation Gladio…

05:20 Would you believe us if we told you that,  following the end of the Second World War,

05:24 armed resistance operatives were carrying out  clandestine missions in European countries?

05:28 No it wasn’t remnants of the Nazi party  or the USSR… it was the United States.

05:33 Codenamed Operation Gladio, these covert  missions were a direct collaboration between

05:38 the personnel of what would become the Central  Intelligence Agency, NATO, and the Western Union.

05:43 Operation Gladio consisted mainly of ‘stay behind’  operations - This involved countries embedding

05:48 sleeper agents in their own territories,  who would lie in wait to be deployed in the

05:53 event of an enemy invasion from nations like the  Soviet Union, which was steadily amassing power.

05:59 These stay-behind operatives would  establish resistance movements

06:02 within their home countries, then, should a  Soviet onslaught roll in, they’d stay put,

06:07 and work as spies from behind enemy lines. So, what did Operation Gladio actually entail?

06:12 Operatives were used to carry out political  assassinations, psychological warfare,

06:17 and false flag operations, essentially,  a smorgasbord of nefarious deeds,

06:21 against left wing parties in Western Europe. This  often meant aligning with anti-communist militias

06:27 and right wing terrorists as Gladio’s network of  secret operatives captured, tortured, and killed

06:32 anyone suspected of having communist leanings. To this day though, the US Department of State

06:36 denies the truth that their own operatives were  backing terrorist groups, and that Gladio was

06:41 only a way to aid Western European countries  from resisting a potential Soviet invasion.

06:46 But the CIA messing with Europe is one  thing - what about the FBI killing dozens

06:51 of Americans back in the good old US of A? During the Prohibition Era, the FBI was involved

06:57 in trying to develop ways to prevent bootleggers  from brewing illegal alcohol. In order to do that,

07:02 they increased the amount of methanol, a poisonous  substance found in the same industrial alcohol

07:07 that bootleggers would use to make liquor. While  intended to discourage people from drinking,

07:12 this increase led to thousands of deaths. For over a decade, the United States banned

07:17 both the sale and production of drinking  alcohol, and federal law enforcement devoted

07:22 significant resources to tackling the illegal  attempts people made to circumvent these laws.

07:27 Speakeasies and smuggling networks were primary  targets for law enforcement, as was bootlegging,

07:32 which had itself become a lucrative business  for organized crime syndicates. But the moment

07:37 one operation was busted, another  quickly appeared to take its place.

07:41 To limit the publicly available supply of alcohol,  law enforcement and federal regulators devised a

07:46 new strategy. As bootleg alcohol was typically  produced by distilling industrial alcohols,

07:51 US officials figured that, if it became  legally mandated that toxic additives had

07:56 to be included in these products, then they  could cut off the supply before consumption.

08:01 So, the US Treasury Department  ordered companies to add quinine,

08:04 methyl alcohol and additional toxic chemicals  to industrial alcohol as a deterrent.

08:09 A deterrent that didn’t work. On Christmas Eve of 1926, 60 people

08:14 were admitted to the Bellevue Hospital in New York  as a result of poisoned alcohol - 31 of which died

08:20 in the next few days. Many had inadvertently  consumed methanol, industrial strength alcohol

08:25 that was legal under federal law, but extremely  poisonous. And that’s just a snapshot of the

08:30 staggering number of deaths that occurred as a  result of alcohol poisoned by these chemicals.

08:35 While it’s often misinterpreted that the  FBI deliberately poisoned drinking alcohol,

08:39 it can’t be understated the unethical lengths  that the United States’ federal government went

08:43 to in order to curb public consumption  of alcohol and illegal bootlegging.

08:48 They might not have been dropping  mercury into bottles of whiskey,

08:51 but the US government did increase the level of  toxic chemicals present in industrial alcohols,

08:57 knowing full well that these were being used  distilled in order to be sold and drunk.

09:01 Speaking of incredibly dangerous things to put  into your body… Ever heard of Project MKNAOMI?

09:06 The now infamous Project MKULTRA is often  cited when talking about crazy conspiracies,

09:11 but its successor often flies under the  radar. Project MKNAOMI was a joint operation

09:17 between the CIA and the US Department of  Defense that ran for almost two decades,

09:22 between the fifties and the late sixties.

09:24 The goal of Project MKNAOMI was to conduct  research into chemical and biological warfare,

09:29 specifically determining what substances  and chemicals could be used to either kill

09:34 or incapacitate a target… and then developing  devices that could diffuse these materials.

09:39 While MKULTRA had a strong emphasis on mind  control experiments, MKNAOMI focused on ways

09:45 to weaponize bacteria and viruses, knockout  gases, lethal poisons, and delivery systems

09:51 that could be used to administer them. The CIA’s Technical Services Division was

09:55 tasked with developing a whole arsenal  of lethal or incapacitating materials,

09:59 with the US Army’s Special Operations Command  assigned to assist with the testing. Afterall,

10:04 what are friends for? Perhaps most notably,  MKNAOMI led to the creation of a number of

10:09 guns that were modified to fire darts coated in  deadly biological agents. These were strong enough

10:15 to incapacitate guard dogs, allowing covert agents  to infiltrate an area; then, a remedial chemical

10:21 agent could be used to reawaken the dogs upon the  agents’ exit, covering their tracks as they left.

10:27 While officially declassified information  about Project MKNAOMI is hard to come by,

10:31 a CIA memo that proposed using biological  weapons to target crops was uncovered in

10:36 1967 by the Church Committee - and we’ve  got more about what else that committee

10:41 revealed to the world coming up shortly. After this memo was discovered, President

10:45 Richard Nixon was forced to ban the military  use of biological weapons in November 1969,

10:51 and Project MKNAOMI was dissolved. However,  despite the president’s orders, in 1970, one rogue

10:57 CIA scientist stole approximately eleven grams  of a deadly shellfish toxin with help from SOC

11:04 personnel at Fort Detrick, Maryland. This  dangerous toxin was then stashed in a CIA

11:09 owned lab, going undetected for over five years. But it’s not just the US that gets involved

11:15 in sinister secret plots. Sometimes, it’s US  allies. Such was the case in The Lavon Affair.

11:21 While arguably not as infamous as the likes  of Gladio, or other US led covert operations,

11:26 the Lavon Affair was no less deplorable. Planned  by the Israeli Military Intelligence in 1954,

11:32 under the innocuous codename of Operation  Susannah, this was a false flag operation.

11:38 During the summer of 1954, a group of Egyptian  Jewish people were recruited by Israel’s military

11:44 intelligence to attack multiple civilian targets  in Egypt. These included Egyptian, American and

11:49 British owned businesses, cinemas, libraries and  US educational centers throughout the country.

11:55 These recruits were instructed to plant bombs  in these establishments, and upon detonation,

12:00 the attacks were to be pinned on communists, the  Muslim Brotherhood – a Sunni Islamist organization

12:05 in Egypt – or unspecified local nationalists. The operation began when the sleeper cell,

12:10 consisting of eight Egyptian Jews, bombed the  post office in Alexandria. Within weeks, six other

12:16 buildings were also targeted, with the Egyptian  government eventually being tipped off – allegedly

12:21 by the person overseeing the operation – about  where the next bombing was planned to take place.

12:26 With that information, they were able to swoop in  and arrest the bomber, then capturing the entire

12:31 covert Israeli cell of eleven suspects. While the  bombings didn’t result in any civilian deaths,

12:36 four of the operatives died, two of them after  being captured and another two being sentenced

12:40 to execution by the Egyptian government.  Two more were acquitted at their trial,

12:45 and the remaining five received varying prison  sentences that ranged from seven years to life.

12:50 But the lingering question in all this is why?  Well, the intent of this failed false flag was

12:55 to pin the blame on organizations that opposed  Egypt’s leader, Gamal Abdel Nasser. It was hoped

13:00 that the subsequent chaos would convince Western  governments that Nasser’s regime over Egypt was

13:05 unstable, and therefore prompting these nations  to withdraw any financial or military support.

13:10 After the operation failed, Israeli defence  minister Pinhas Lavon was implicated in

13:14 orchestrating the bombing attacks and was  consequently forced to resign, leading to the

13:19 incident being referred to as the Lavon Affair.  Israel continued to publicly deny that they’d

13:24 had any involvement in the Lavon Affair until  as recently as 2005; the surviving Egyptian

13:29 agents who had been involved in the attacks were  awarded certificates of appreciation by the then

13:33 President of Israel, Moshe Katsav - the covert  agent equivalent of a participation medal.

13:39 But that isn’t the last piece of military  subterfuge we’ve got on the docket today.

13:43 Far from it, in fact. So let’s dive into  the infamous Gulf War Syndrome cover up.

13:47 Following the end of the Gulf War – which took  place between 1990 and 1991 – a concerning number

13:53 of veterans who had fought in the conflict  reported developing unusual symptoms after

13:57 returning home. Reports came in from Gulf  War veterans in the United States, Canada,

14:01 Austria and Denmark. But for those returning  home to the UK and suffering from this strange

14:06 Gulf War Syndrome, the health issues they  reported would be suspiciously silenced…

14:11 In every reported case, soldiers who  had been previously fit and healthy

14:15 seemed to suddenly develop a litany of  unusual illnesses and symptoms. These

14:19 ranged from experiencing chronic fatigue,  hypertension, muscle pain, cognitive issues,

14:24 a lack of coordination, outbreaks of  rashes and other skin conditions, diarrhea,

14:29 as well as symptoms related to  Post Traumatic Stress Disorder.

14:32 What made this so unusual though, compared to the  illnesses suffered by veterans of previous wars,

14:37 was that there seemed to be a much higher rate  of symptoms and at much greater intensity among

14:42 those who’d fought in the Gulf War. The primary  cause that’s been attributed to this is exposure

14:47 to sub-lethal amounts of chemical warfare  agents, particularly nerve gas, as well

14:52 as the inhalation of smoke from oil well fires,  and exposure to pesticides and depleted uranium.

14:58 In the United Kingdom, several assessments  of the affected veterans were carried out to

15:01 determine if there was any link between those  experiencing these symptoms. But Kings College

15:06 London was unable to determine any common  causality among sufferers. Meanwhile, other

15:11 countries like the United States were quicker to  recognize the existence of this Gulf War Syndrome.

15:15 The UK’s Ministry of Defence vehemently denied  that such a condition existed, despite the

15:20 overwhelming evidence among veterans from the  Gulf War. They would eventually relent in 2005,

15:25 and subsequent research was conducted in 2009  that further confirmed Gulf War veterans were

15:30 more likely to report symptoms compared to other  veterans. They were also twice as likely to have

15:35 suffered from PTSD and reported a poorer  quality of life following their service.

15:40 However, as recently as 2010, an overwhelming  majority of the UK’s Gulf War veterans hadn’t

15:45 received any form of compensation from their  government and claims for war pensions have been

15:50 denied to those who served in the Gulf War and  reported to be suffering with Gulf War Syndrome.

15:55 Sometimes, governments conspire to shaft large  groups of people. Sometimes, it’s just one very

16:00 unfortunate dude. Welcome to The Dreyfus Affair The Dreyfus Affair took place in France between

16:05 the late nineteenth and early twentieth  centuries. It surrounded one Alfred Dreyfus,

16:10 an artillery captain within the French army.  In 1894, after a seemingly damning letter of

16:15 evidence was discovered, Dreyfus was accused of  selling French military secrets to Germany and was

16:20 convicted of treason… Wrongly convicted. Working in the German Embassy in Paris,

16:25 a French spy named Major Hubert-Joseph Henry  uncovered a partially ripped up letter in a

16:30 waste basket. The handwriting that had been used  to pen the letter resembled that of Dreyfus,

16:35 leading to what would become a controversial  arrest and accusation levied against the man. The

16:40 public were quick to believe the charges slammed  against Dreyfus owed purely to the fact that he

16:44 was Jewish. Antisemitic groups in France at the  time amplified the notion of his guilt, especially

16:50 the newspaper La Libre Parole, which claimed that  Dreyfus exemplified the disloyalty of French Jews.

16:56 Dreyfus was court-martialed and sentenced to life  in prison on Devil’s Island, located off the coast

17:01 of French Guiana. In a harrowing public ceremony  following his conviction, he had the French army’s

17:06 insignia torn off his uniform and his sword  broken before being paraded in front of a crowd

17:12 who hurled antisemitic insults at him and even  called for Dreyfus to be executed for treason.

17:18 However, in 1896, evidence would come to light  that implicated a different French officer, named

17:23 Ferdinand Walsin-Esterhazy, as the true traitor.  This started swaying public support for Dreyfus,

17:29 but after Esterhazy’s subsequent court martial, he  was quickly found not guilty and fled the country.

17:34 Dreyfus was court-martialed a second  time in 1899, and found guilty again,

17:39 yet France was still deeply divided over the case.  Days later, Dreyfus received a full pardon from

17:44 the French president, and then in 1906 he would  be fully exonerated and reinstated into the army.

17:50 Antisemitism is undeniably a horrible  blight on the planet. Just like nuclear

17:54 war. And what do we have to thank for  that? The Manhattan Project, of course!

17:58 In a post Oppenheimer world, almost  everyone’s heard of the Manhattan Project,

18:02 the infamous World War Two collaborative  research and development program between

18:06 the United States, United Kingdom and Canada  that produced the very first nuclear weapons,

18:11 irreversibly altering the course of history. Between 1942 and 1946, the project resulted in two

18:17 distinct types of bombs; the Thin Man, a fission  based nuclear weapon, and the Little Boy, the

18:22 more complex, implosion type nuclear weapon, both  designed by nuclear physicist and the destroyer

18:28 of worlds himself, J. Robert Oppenheimer. But at the time, public knowledge about the

18:32 Manhattan Project was severely limited. The goal  of security officials linked to the Manhattan

18:37 Project was to keep word about the development of  atomic bombs from reaching Nazi Germany and their

18:42 Axis power allies, in particular Japan, who would  suffer the first ever nuclear attacks in history

18:48 as a direct result of the Manhattan Project. Details of the program were also kept a secret

18:52 from the Soviet Union; despite the USSR being  aligned with the USA, UK and other Allied Forces,

18:58 the United States regarded them as a potential  future enemy. However, some Soviet spies were

19:03 successful in infiltrating the Manhattan  Project headquarters in Los Alamos, and

19:07 disseminated information about the program back  to Russia, which helped speed up the development

19:12 of the Soviets’ very own nuclear bombs. There were also a surprising amount of

19:16 leaks during the 1940s from American journalists,  some of them small and inconsequential, but others

19:21 far more damning. Around the time of the Second  World War, the United States operated a program of

19:26 voluntary press censorship that allowed its Office  of Censorship to… sternly rebuke journalists that

19:32 reported on a list of prohibited topics. Essentially, any censorship that took place

19:36 usually went into effect after important  information had already been published.

19:41 One of the worst violations in relation  to the Manhattan Project occurred in 1944,

19:46 when a reporter for the Cleveland Press, the  unfortunately named John Raper, discovered that

19:51 a military operation was occurring in Los Alamos  while he had been on vacation in New Mexico. Raper

19:57 had no idea that atomic bombs were being developed  there, but he erroneously reported the location

20:02 and approximate size of a classified military  science facility, n provided local witness

20:07 accounts of explosives being tested on the site,  and worst of all, he named Oppenheimer as the

20:12 scientific director of the Manhattan Project. At the behest of Major General Leslie Groves,

20:17 the US Army’s director of the Manhattan Project,  the Office of Censorship was able to prevent

20:22 any follow up articles being published. This  included one being planned by Time magazine,

20:26 to ensure further information about the project  couldn’t be spread any further. Groves also

20:31 considered drafting John Raper in retaliation for  his article, only relenting when he learned that

20:36 the journalist was in his sixties, and hardly at  a prime age to be forced into military service.

20:41 Next up is a scientific study  that breached moral and ethical

20:44 boundaries on a truly unprecedented scale. The Tuskegee Syphilis Experiment was a study

20:49 that ran from 1932 until 1972. Funded by the  United States government and carried out by the US

20:56 Public Health Service and the Centers for Disease  Control and Prevention, the goal of the research

21:01 project was to examine the effects and symptoms  of syphilis when left untreated. And at the time,

21:06 there was no known cure for the disease. In order to make their observations, the

21:10 Public Health Service enrolled around six hundred  impoverished African American sharecroppers - 399

21:16 with syphilis and 201 without - many of whom had  never even visited a doctor before. They were

21:23 enticed by an offer of free medical care, however  the people behind the study intentionally refused

21:28 to explain exactly what they were examining in the  men that would unwittingly become test subjects.

21:34 Those participating in the Tuskegee  Experiment were falsely told they were

21:37 being treated for ‘bad blood’, a colloquial,  non-specific term used in the area to

21:43 describe a number of different ailments. The participants were given placebos such

21:47 as aspirin and mineral supplements, and told  that this would treat their condition. However,

21:51 some fifteen years into the study, in 1947,  a treatment for syphilis was discovered in

21:57 the form of penicillin. The Public Health  Service neglected to tell these men the

22:01 truth at any point, nor did they offer the  widely available antibiotic which had since

22:05 become the standard treatment for syphilis. In fact, the researchers offered no medical

22:10 care to these men as their condition progressed,  even as some of them started to go blind, suffered

22:15 other severe health problems or even went insane  due to syphilis. Over the course of the study,

22:20 28 participants passed away due to syphilis, and  a further one hundred died from complications

22:26 linked to the disease. Forty of the participants’  spouses were also diagnosed with it, and it had

22:31 been passed on to almost twenty children. A year after the story broke and sparked

22:35 public outrage, Congress held multiple hearings  looking into the Tuskegee Experiment. In 1974,

22:41 the surviving participants of the unethical  study, along with the families of those who

22:45 had died, received a ten million dollar  settlement, and new guidelines were put

22:49 in place in order to protect human subjects. And that would be the last time the US was ever

22:54 involved in a sinister cover up… Okay, we lied,  that sentence was, in itself, a cover up. Gotta

22:59 earn those secretive US government checks somehow! Adding yet another US political scandal to this

23:04 list, the Iran Contra Affair saw the United  States’ National Security Council becoming

23:09 involved in several secret arms deals without the  knowledge or approval of Congress. As a matter of

23:13 fact, these transactions were outright banned  by congress, and violated the government’s own

23:18 policies. Through the NSC, the US traded missiles  and other weapons to free American hostages in

23:23 Lebanon, as well as channeling funds to support  an armed conflict that was occurring in Nicaragua.

23:29 The Iran Contra Affair was so controversial  that it even threatened to topple the

23:33 President of the US at the time, Ronald Reagan. After Reagan – a Republican – took office, his

23:38 political reach was limited by a Democrat majority  in the House of Representatives, and the US

23:43 Senate. But one of his major political platforms  had been to back the numerous anti-Communist

23:48 insurgencies that were operating around the globe,  something that the Democrats wouldn’t support. In

23:53 fact, they actively brought in legislation to  limit the influence the CIA and the Department

23:58 of Defence had on foreign conflicts. At the time, both Iran and Nicaragua

24:02 had undergone significant changes to their  regimes, with the former toppling their

24:06 pro Western government, replacing it with an  anti-US Islamic fundamentalist one. Meanwhile,

24:11 the latter was now under the control  of the leftist Sandinista government,

24:15 who Reagan and his administration feared would  allow communism to spread into Central America.

24:20 So, without the approval of Congress,  financial and military support was

24:23 offered by the US to the Contras, the counter  revolutionary forces that were attempting to

24:28 overthrow Nicaragua’s left wing government. They attempted to pull off a similar strategy

24:33 in Iran, however things were complicated when  the Iran Hostage Crisis took place. During which,

24:38 Iranian backed Shi’ite terrorists took a number  of American diplomats and private contractors

24:43 hostage. In order to secure the release of the  hostages, the NSC engaged in an arms deal with

24:48 Iran, with plans to also channel the funds from  that deal to the Contras insurgents in Nicaragua.

24:54 These illegal arms trading activities were  discovered in November of 1986, when a plane

24:59 that was carrying supplies to the Contras was  shot down by the Sandinistas, and the pilot was

25:03 taken prisoner. Naturally, a public uproar quickly  followed in the US once this was brought to light.

25:09 But that’s nowhere near as freaky as what  went on… In Operation Midnight Climax.

25:15 While MKULTRA’s name lives in infamy, the  codename of Operation Midnight Climax is

25:20 often forgotten about. This was a sub project of  MKULTRA, specifically its mind control research

25:25 program that started in the fifties. The  man in charge was one Sidney Gottleib,

25:30 a CIA chemist and spymaster who was permitted to  test Lysergic acid diethylamide, commonly known

25:36 as LSD on civilians… without their consent. Gottlieb was also that rogue CIA scientist we

25:43 mentioned who stole all the shellfish poison  earlier. Yes, this will be relevant later.

25:48 Anyway, back to Midnight Climax. The CIA paid escorts to lure their

25:52 clients into safehouses, where they were  administered with a wide and dangerous array

25:56 of substances without their knowledge,  and observed from behind one-way-glass.

26:01 The unwilling participants were  pressed to reveal personal secrets,

26:05 fed subliminal messages to make them carry  out actions involuntarily, including seeing

26:10 whether under the influence of LSD they could be  convinced to carry out assaults, robberies and

26:15 even assassinations. The goal was for the CIA to  determine if brainwashing was possible, and how

26:20 to gain control over the minds of enemy spies. They also wanted to test whether LSD could be

26:25 used during interrogations, and combined the drug  with intense isolation, dosing subjects and then

26:31 keeping them confined and alone for months at  a time, with hardly any food or water. Hundreds

26:36 of federal agents and scientists took part  in these unethical experiments on innocent

26:41 people before Operation Midnight Climax, and the  rest of MKULTRA, was shut down in the sixties.

26:47 But we know what you’ve all been waiting  for… The deranged CIA secret weapon.

26:52 Arguably the most infamous and unusual finding  of the Church Committee was the CIA’s very own

26:58 ‘Heart Attack Gun’. This secret weapon wasn’t  just a concept either, it was very real,

27:03 and used in multiple assassinations. It worked  by firing a small poison dart filled with frozen

27:08 shellfish toxin - hmm, wonder where they got that  - that would then trigger a heart attack in its

27:13 target. The darts could easily pierce clothing,  and would be hardly felt by the target, leaving

27:18 little more than a small red dot on the skin. The darts would completely disintegrate when

27:23 entering the target’s body, leaving little trace,  and allowing the poison to rapidly entire their

27:27 bloodstream, causing a fatal heart attack.  After death, the poison denatures quickly,

27:32 meaning detecting it in an autopsy is next  to impossible, causing the death to be

27:36 chalked up to completely natural causes. The existence of this almost fictitious

27:41 sounding weapon was revealed during the Church  Committee’s investigations and was verified by

27:46 Congressional testimony on the CIA’s many  rogue espionage activities. You can even

27:51 find photos of Senator Church himself  holding the infamous Heart Attack Gun.

27:56 Now check out “Inside the CIA’s Terrifying  ‘Sleep Room’.” Or watch this video instead!

docs.text:
00:00 The 9/11 terror attacks scarred a  nation - and even decades later,

00:04 some things still don’t add  up. Like who knew about it?

00:07 Was there insider trading? And the  case of a strange disappearance...

00:11 Find out the answer to these mysteries and more

00:13 on this episode of The Infographics Show -  “Things About 9/11 That Don’t Make Sense”.

00:18 September 11th, 2001.

00:20 The world was shocked as coordinated  terror attacks hit the United States.

00:23 Members of Osama Bin Laden’s Al Qaeda terrorist  cult hijacked planes, using them as weapons

00:29 to hit high-profile targets.Two jets slammed  into the World Trade Center in New York City,

00:34 killing over 2,000 people and reducing the iconic  towers to rubble. A third plane hit the Pentagon,

00:39 killing hundreds. And a fourth - headed  for the Capitol Building - was brought

00:43 down in a Pennsylvania field by the  heroic actions of its passengers.

00:47 It was the deadliest terror attack in history.

00:49 Everyone knows someone who questions the official  story of 9/11. They usually have an elaborate rant

00:55 about how jet fuel can’t melt steel beams. And  when you question them on what actually happened,

01:00 they’ll tell you “The lizard people just  want us to think the towers blew up.” Those

01:05 conspiracies have been explored and debunked  many times over. But over twenty years later,

01:09 there’s still some things that just don’t  make sense about the horrifying day.

01:14 #9.

01:15 For one thing, the entire circumstances of the  attack seem surreal to those who grew up in its

01:20 aftermath. Unlike most terror attacks since, the  attack was extremely low-tech. The terrorists,

01:25 organized in groups of four or five,  boarded planes holding only box cutters.

01:30 They took the plane hostage, forced the  pilot to give up control or killed them,

01:34 and piloted the plane into its intended  target. It seems like a well-planned - if

01:39 simple - operation. But there’s one  thing that still raises some eyebrows.

01:43 Why did Mohammed Atta travel to Portland,  Maine the night before the attack?

01:48 On September 10th, 2001, Mohamed Atta picked  up his fellow hijacker Abdul-Azzia Al-Omari

01:54 at a hotel in Boston. From there, they drove a  rented car north to Portland - almost two hours

02:00 away. Surveillance footage captured the pair  checking into a Portland hotel that evening.

02:04 They were also seen making ATM withdrawals,  browsing the aisles of a local Wal-Mart,

02:08 and in the parking lot of a nearby Pizza Hut. Some believe Atta was conducting surveillance

02:13 detection, making sure no one was tailing him.  Others think it was a strategic move - security

02:17 at Portland’s airport may have been lighter than  Boston’s. Another theory was he was planning

02:22 for last-minute delays or meeting with an  unknown accomplice. Whatever the reason,

02:27 on the morning of September 11th, Atta boarded a  flight back to Boston. Once he landed, he received

02:32 a call from Marwan Al-Shehi, another 9/11 hijacker  - believed to be the green light for the attacks.

02:37 Atta would go on to hijack American Airlines  Flight 11, crashing it into the North Tower.

02:42 Despite years of investigation, Atta’s trip to  Portland remains one of the most mysterious pieces

02:47 of the 9/11 puzzle.

02:50 One of the scariest things about 9/11 was the  uncertainty in the immediate aftermath. Thousands

02:55 of people died - but very few bodies were found.  Almost all the casualties in New York and on the

03:00 planes were essentially vaporized, with their  families desperately seeking any evidence of

03:04 their loved ones’ so they could have some degree  of closure. Many disappeared without a trace.

03:10 One was Sneha Anne Phillip, an  Indian-American physician who

03:13 was last seen on September 10th  near her home in Lower Manhattan,

03:17 shopping at a department store. She  likely made her purchases and went home.

03:20 And then, no trace of her was ever seen again.

03:23 Unlike most of the 9/11 victims, there are no  reports of her being on-site, and no eye-witnesses

03:29 ever reported seeing her. Her family has reason  to believe she was there - she was a physician,

03:34 and may have gone to the World Trade Center to  offer medical assistance. But few of the doctors

03:38 who were on-site went into the towers themselves.  Instead, they were helping people who were injured

03:43 after escaping. And while people did die on  the ground due to falling debris and fires,

03:48 those were the bodies most likely to be recovered  intact. Multiple investigations by the NYPD and a

03:53 private investigation commissioned by  Phillip’s husband turned up nothing.

03:57 Which has led many people to  wonder - is everything as it seems?

04:01 Phillip had a troubled past before the events  of 9/11, being fired from her job at Cabrini

04:06 Medical Center due to tardiness and alcoholism.  She complained to police that an intern groped

04:11 her during a staff night out. The case would  later be dropped and Phillip was charged with

04:15 filing a false police report. It seemed like  her life was spiraling before the terror attack.

04:20 Could she have faked her  death or died in another way,

04:23 and it was completely ignored in  the chaos of the terror attack?

04:26 Her family has been suing to have her  officially confirmed as a victim of the

04:30 9/11 attacks, allowing her to be  honored officially. And in 2008,

04:34 an appeals court gave them their wish and  she was added to the Ground Zero Memorial.

04:39 That’s the legal outcome - but any hard  evidence remains painfully hard to come by.

04:43 And in the immediate aftermath, confusion reigned.

04:47 #7.

04:48 Osama Bin Laden and his Al Qaeda terror network  quickly claimed responsibility for the attacks,

04:53 and he became the world’s public enemy #1. But  he came from a very big family - the son of a

04:59 billionaire Saudi oil baron who had multiple  wives and 50 children. And he was considered

05:04 the black sheep - most of his family were  jet-setting businesspeople, with devoutly

05:08 Muslim beliefs. They had no affiliation to terror  groups and viewed Osama as a disgrace. In 2001,

05:14 the Bin Laden family was spread around  the world… including in the United States.

05:18 It was one of the strangest affairs that  took place in the days after the attacks.

05:22 Flights were grounded for two days, and strictly  regulated after that. And it would be several

05:28 weeks before one of the most controversial  flights to happen in that time was revealed.

05:32 On September 13th, twelve members of the  Bin Laden family who were in the U.S. were

05:37 put on a plane and evacuated back to  Saudi Arabia. When this was revealed,

05:41 it caused some outrage - why were the  relatives of our enemy being evacuated?

05:46 And many asked - why were they such a priority?

05:49 This was conspiracy fodder of the highest degree,  with some arguing it showed that the government

05:54 was in on the attacks or at least collaborating  with the Bin Laden family. But less conspiratorial

05:59 individuals said that most of the Bin Ladens  in the country were high school and college

06:03 students. And besides, money talks - reportedly  the evacuations were kick-started when one of

06:08 Bin Laden’s brothers sought help from the Saudi  Embassy. Saudi Arabia had good relations with

06:13 the Bush administration, thanks to their many oil  deals and geopolitical significance. The likely

06:18 scenario is that they were evacuated for their  protection due to fears of reprisals, but it

06:24 still raised some eyebrows - and the government  has been tight-lipped about it ever since.

06:28 But one figure might be at the center of it all.

06:31 #6.

06:32 The biggest question regarding 9/11 has  always been “who knew”? The most common

06:37 suspect has been George W. Bush. Many people  insist that the US President must have known

06:41 in advance and allowed the attacks to  happen so he would have an excuse for

06:45 war. There’s no evidence for that - but  his close ties to the Saudi government

06:49 continue to draw scrutiny. Almost all  the hijackers were from Saudi Arabia,

06:54 and so was one of the most mysterious figures  related to the attacks, Omar Al-Bayouni.

06:59 Did this Saudi intelligence  agent know what was coming?

07:02 Although of Egyptian descent, Al-Bayouni’s  family had settled in Saudi Arabia,

07:06 where he became a well-connected  figure with reported ties to the

07:09 Saudi government. He also reportedly had  close ties to known terrorist associates,

07:14 including helping two of the eventual  hijackers find housing in San Diego.

07:18 And by the time the attacks hit, he was gone.

07:21 He was in the UK pursuing a PhD when  the towers fell, and ten days later,

07:25 he was arrested in a joint US-British operation.  The evidence of his links to terrorist associates

07:30 was strong, including many phone calls to a  key Bin Laden associate, Ziyad Khaleel and

07:36 Saudi Ministry of Islamic Affairs cleric Fahad  al-Thumairy. Al-Thumairy denied knowing Bayoumi,

07:42 despite telephone records showing at least 60  calls between them. But the British weren’t

07:47 able to produce any hard evidence of his knowledge  or involvement, and they ultimately released him.

07:52 He would soon return to Saudi  Arabia…and disappear off the map

07:56 completely. His association with the  attack has never been fully proven,

07:59 but an FBI report indicates that they  believe there’s a better-than-even chance

08:04 he was a conspirator. But if anyone wants  answers, they’ll have to find him first.

08:09 But there’s one site on Ground Zero that  causes more controversy than any other.

08:13 #5.

08:14 In late 2000, two of the 9/11 hijackers -  Khalid Almihdhar and Nawaf Alhazmi - rented

08:20 a room in San Diego from a man who  was an undercover FBI informant.

08:25 The informant - whose identity has never  been released to the public - was a tested

08:29 asset for the Bureau. He prayed with the  two men and helped them adjust to life

08:33 in the U.S. - he even assisted one of them in  opening a bank account. But he never provided

08:38 their names to his FBI handler. And perhaps more  importantly, the handler never asked. At the time,

08:44 Almihdhar and Alhazmi were already persons  of interest to the CIA, having attended an

08:48 al-Qaeda summit in Malaysia just months earlier. The pair moved into the informant’s house in

08:53 September 2000. Almihdhar moved out six weeks  later, and Alhazmi left by the end of the

08:58 year. During that time, both men attended flight  school in preparation for the devastating attack.

09:03 It wasn’t until after the 9/11 attacks  that the informant recognized the names

09:07 being reported in the media. He called his  handler and revealed that the hijackers

09:11 had been his roommates. There’s no evidence he  intentionally concealed their identities - but

09:15 it still remains a glaring example of  miscommunication between intelligence agencies.

09:20 A CIA alert naming the two men as potential  terrorists had been issued on August 23,

09:26 2001. But by then, the opportunity was gone. As  one counterintelligence expert later queried, why

09:32 didn’t the agent ask more questions? Or at least  explore the possibility of recruiting new assets?

09:38 And it wasn’t the only  mystery that lingered on 9/11.

09:41 #4.

09:42 He’s called the “last person  killed in New York on 9/11”,

09:46 but he wasn’t a worker in the towers or a  first-responder. His name was Henryk Siwiak,

09:51 and he was a Polish immigrant minding his  own business in the Brooklyn neighborhood of

09:55 Bedford-Stuyvesant. A former Polish government  worker, he was visiting his sister in New York

10:00 and decided to get a job to send money back to  his family. While he didn’t speak much English,

10:04 he was a hard worker and managed to  get a job as a construction worker.

10:07 But on that fateful day, he  would meet a shocking end.

10:10 After his job site shut down for  the day after the terror attacks,

10:14 he walked across the Brooklyn Bridge and went to  interview for a job cleaning a local supermarket.

10:18 Through a series of miscommunications,  he was given the wrong directions for the

10:22 store address, and went to what was a fairly  dangerous, crime-ridden neighborhood. There,

10:27 eyewitnesses reported hearing an argument,  followed by some gunshots. Siwiak was found

10:32 on the pavement, bleeding out from  a fatal gunshot wound to the chest.

10:36 And over 20 years later, his  murder has never been solved.

10:40 Not surprisingly, this was mostly attributed  to one thing - the police were completely

10:44 occupied by the massive terror attack  in Manhattan. It left zero resources for

10:48 investigating a routine homicide. This has  led Siwiak’s case to gain extra notoriety,

10:53 but even in the best of times, a murder  where the murder weapon is never found

10:56 is extremely hard to solve. But there  were other odd factors to the killing,

11:01 such as the fact that no money was taken from  Siwiak. Did his killer think the mild-mannered

11:05 foreign man may have been involved with the  attack? The cold case is only getting colder.

11:10 And it’s far from the only false accusation  of involvement that has cropped up.

11:14 #3.

11:15 While some conspiracy theories relating to 9/11  are more outlandish - with people claiming the

11:20 towers were destroyed by explosives planted by the  government - most of them simply focus on who to

11:26 blame. In the immediate aftermath of the attacks,  a lot of suspects, including the U.S. government,

11:31 had fingers pointed at them. But in later years,  conspiracies focused on another target - Israel,

11:37 who were among the greatest enemies of Osama  Bin Laden. And people who insist they must

11:42 have been involved even point to some specific  targets - the so-called “Dancing Israelis”.

11:47 So what has made this theory stick around so long?

11:50 First off, there’s no evidence that anyone  else was involved in 9/11 besides Osama Bin

11:56 Laden and his network of terrorists - he  proudly took credit for the attacks. But

12:00 some people insist that a group of Israelis was  arrested near the towers a short time after 9/11,

12:06 reportedly laughing and celebrating the attacks.

12:09 There’s no evidence of how they were acting -  but a deep dive into government files did reveal

12:14 six Israeli nationals were arrested in lower  Manhattan, and later deported back to Israel.

12:19 It’s believed that the six men were  likely Israeli intelligence agents,

12:22 here collecting information on the attacks.  Israel viewed Al Qaeda as a serious security

12:27 threat at the time. Many countries likely  have spies in the country at all times,

12:31 and it only becomes a serious issue when they’re  trying to access secret or high-risk information.

12:36 But in the immediate aftermath of  9/11, security stepped up big time

12:40 and deported a lot of people who may  have been slipping under the radar.

12:44 And so they went back - leaving a trail  of decades-long conspiracies behind them.

12:49 But if there’s one question that’s been lingering  all these years, it’s this - did anyone know?

12:54 #2.

12:54 Some of the more outlandish conspiracy theories  claim that the attacks were masterminded in the

12:58 United States, but most simply allege that it  was allowed to proceed without being reported.

13:03 Some claim the government wanted to have an  excuse to start a war in the Middle East,

13:07 while others claim a massive insurance scam on the  World Trade Center. But no evidence has emerged of

13:12 advanced knowledge by the top power brokers at the  time - but it did emerge in a very unlikely place.

13:18 A high-school classroom.

13:20 It was September 6th, 2001, and English  teacher Antoinette DiLorenzo was greeting

13:25 a new year of students. Her class was  heavily composed of Pakistani immigrants,

13:29 and one of the boys made a disturbing comment  to his Bensonhurst classmates. He claimed that

13:34 the World Trade Center wouldn’t be standing  next week. She chalked it up to a bad-taste

13:39 teenage joke - but then watched in horror as  the prophecy came true. She quickly called

13:43 the authorities, and the FBI and NYPD  tracked the boy down to interrogate him.

13:48 So did this boy have advanced knowledge  of the world’s deadliest terror attack?

13:52 All these years later, we don’t have a clear  answer. The boy claimed he was only joking,

13:57 and his family backed him up - but the coincidence  was such that many people were dubious. The police

14:02 ultimately decided that it was just a case of  the world’s worst-timed joke and no charges

14:07 were ever filed. The most convincing  evidence was that none of the hijackers

14:11 involved in the attack were of Pakistani  background. Fifteen were from Saudi Arabia,

14:16 two were from the United Arab Emirates,  one from Lebanon, and one from Egypt.

14:21 That makes the connections needed for this random  boy to overhear talk about it much less likely.

14:26 But maybe the most bizarre story to  come out of 9/11 indicates that a

14:30 lot of people may have known - and  they made a lot of money off it.

14:35 #1.

14:36 Was there insider trading on 9/11?

14:38 It’s one of the biggest scourges of the insurance  world - people who have advance knowledge of an

14:43 event profiting off it by making trades on the  stock market. It’s what sent Martha Stewart to

14:48 prison, and many Senators faced allegations  of it during the Covid-19 pandemic. The most

14:53 common source of it is when people who work in a  specific company know that the company is about

14:57 to be sold or make a big announcement. They buy  or sell more shares while the price is right.

15:03 But would anyone sink so low as to profit  off a terror attack - and tell no one?

15:08 It was only a week after the attack  when The Times, a London-based paper,

15:12 announced that it was investigating whether  unusual trades happened as a result of advance

15:17 knowledge of the attacks. A massive number of  shares of insurance companies and airlines were

15:22 sold off before the attack, in countries  in Europe as well as Japan and the US.

15:27 This was especially high in the cases of United  Airlines and American Airlines - the two airlines

15:33 whose planes were used in the hijacking. In fact,  it was the highest amount of these stocks ever

15:37 traded on the Chicago Exchange - and the  investors who sold made millions off it.

15:42 The possibility of insider trading  was raised with the 9/11 commission,

15:46 and the fact-finders eventually found  explanations for the unusual trading.

15:50 Both the trading of United and American  shares, which happened on different days,

15:54 were linked to trading strategies  circulated by investment newsletters.

15:58 There was a thorough investigation by the SEC into  the American-based trades, and by intelligence

16:04 agencies into the foreign trades - but no evidence  of advance knowledge of the attack was found.

16:09 But that didn’t stop the digging.

16:11 As the post-9/11 era wore on, damaged hard  drives were discovered in the ruins of the

16:16 World Trade Center - which were transferred  to an elite data recovery company, Convar,

16:20 for retrieval. The German-based  company conducted an investigation

16:24 for US authorities into possible evidence  of criminal insider trading, and was able

16:29 to restore several hundred hard drives over  the next year. However, the 9/11 committee in

16:33 2003 stated that they had not received any  valuable information from the hard drives.

16:38 With no hard evidence of insider trading, much  of the discussion of the topic has turned on

16:43 speculation. As late as 2010, an independent  report claimed that there were at least thirteen

16:49 informed trades that would only make sense if  the investors knew something big was coming.

16:54 The international team of experts pointed to  an unusual increase in trading activity in the

16:58 days before the attacks. But with no hard  evidence, no one has ever been charged for

17:03 insider trading - and it’s likely they never  will. If someone did know and used it to make

17:08 money rather than dropping a dime, it would be the  biggest scandal in the financial sector’s history.

17:14 What do you think is the most overlooked  detail about 9/11? Share your thoughts below.

17:18 Want to know what happened in 9/11  on that fateful day? Check out “What

17:22 Happened Immediately After 9/11” for  all the grim details. And the good news

17:26 is…we got him. Watch “How SEAL Team Took  Down Osama Bin Laden (Minute by Minute)”

17:31 for the tale of the tape of how  the Al Qaeda leader met his end.
